messages:
anya: Heads up — canary run for flashgraft-v2 shows an unexpected ~18% p95 tail latency regression vs flashx on the 8xA100 pool. kv hit-rate dropped ~5% and we see heavy shared-mem bandwidth saturation (smem ~90-94%).perf-bot: Uploaded trace -> https://perf.example/trace/1750000000 (flame + timeline) ; hotspots: smem_write_lane, ldg.global, kv_eviction.sam: Which workload and config? batch sizes / batching heuristic? any change in pipeline stages recently? anya: Minimal config: adaptive batching, max_batch_tokens=2048, min_batch_size=1, kv_cache= paged, kernel_priority=[flashgraft-v2, flashx], runtime flags: --smem-tiling 32x128 --pipeline-stages 3

Command we used:

```
./run_canary.sh --model gpt-200M --kernel flashgraft-v2 --batching adaptive --max-tokens 2048
```

miguel: smem tiling 32x128 + 3-stage pipeline smells like elevated shared mem pressure for fused kernels. flashgraft preloads more into smem than flashx, so with occupancy down you can hit global mem + kv churn.

tara: we did change default pipeline-stages=3 in the last rollout (CL 5542). It reduced warp divergence on long sequences but bumped smem per-block. Might be interacting badly with paged KV because eviction callback touches global memory under load.

karthik: repro plan — run microbench that isolates attention kernel (no kv) and a separate paged-kv-only workload. If attention microbench shows smem BW regression for flashgraft-v2 but not flashx, it's kernel-level. If paged-kv-only shows thrash, then combined effect is kvcache eviction + smem pressure.

anya: quick numbers from canary (aggregated 1k requests):
- flashx: p50=48ms p95=92ms p99=130ms
- flashgraft-v2: p50=50ms p95=109ms p99=160ms
KV hit-rate: flashx=95.1% flashgraft-v2=90.2% (same traffic)
SMEM utilization (averaged across SMs): flashx=78% flashgraft-v2=92%

perf-bot: microtrace summary attached -> flamegraph shows long runs in `smem_preload_chunk` and `kv_maybe_evict` overlapping. Timeline shows smem_write bursts align with kv eviction spikes.

sam: can you share a small reproducer command for microbench (attention-only)?

anya: yes — use this microbench (defaults pin to the same A100 shape):
```
./bench_attention --model gpt-200M --kernel flashgraft-v2 --seq-len 2048 --batch 1 --iters 200 --trace
```

miguel: also try forcing smem tiling to 16x256 and pipeline-stages=2 to see occupancy effect. small perf knob to flip:
```
export REDWOOD_SMEM_TILE=16x256
export REDWOOD_PIPELINE_STAGES=2
./bench_attention ...
```

karthik: another quick try: set kvcache to keep-hot-entries pinned for 30s to avoid eviction noise during microbench. Flag: `--kv-hot-ttl 30s`.

ci-bot: Spawned job #ci/bench/1750000000-micro (attention-only) -> https://ci.example/jobs/1750000000

perf-bot: Early results from microbench run #1750000000-micro:
- flashgraft-v2 w/ default tiling: p95=115ms smem=93% occupancy=0.55
- flashx w/ default tiling: p95=95ms smem=76% occupancy=0.72
- flashgraft-v2 with TILE=16x256, pipeline=2: p95=98ms smem=70% occupancy=0.70

perf-bot: TL;DR — lowering per-block smem usage increased occupancy and removed the tail regression for flashgraft.

anya: looks like root cause = flashgraft-v2 increases per-block shared memory (preload) which, combined with pipeline-stages=3, reduces occupancy and exposes kv eviction stalls on paged KV. When occupancy drops, the kernel is more sensitive to global stalls triggered by kv_eviction.

sam: proposed action items:
1) short-term: revert pipeline-stages back to 2 for canary cohorts using flashgraft-v2 (rollback flag + config pin)
2) mid-term: add adaptive smem-tiling heuristic that reduces preload when paged KV is enabled or occupancy < 0.65
3) perf test: microbench matrix (tile=16/32, pipeline=2/3, kvhotpin on/off, kernels flashgraft/flashx) — owners: miguel + anya
4) follow-up: consider KV pinning policy improvements and eviction backoff to avoid synchronous eviction during attention hot paths

miguel: I'll take item 3. will run matrix overnight and post a concise table.

anya: I'll open a rollout-blocker PR to pin pipeline-stages=2 for flashgraft nodes and add a runtime guard for the smem-tiling heuristic.

karthik: let's also add a perf regression alert that triggers on p95 delta > 10% for new kernel rollouts and ties to smem/utilization. Otherwise this flakiness will slip through.

anya: agreed. created issue RD-2217 for adaptive tiling + RD-2218 for eviction backoff. linking in PR when I have numbers.

sam: cool. thumbs up — run the matrix and we'll reconvene tomorrow. :thumbsup:
